cause.note: The kernel explicitly names the exact scanner container as the victim of guest-global OOM. This establishes why this scanner disappeared, not which concurrent workload consumed the memory or whether one scanner alone would fit.

dockerEventQuery.interpretation: No historical events were returned by this later query. This is not proof that no OOM, kill, stop or destroy occurred; the kernel evidence independently establishes OOM.

guestPressureStallInformation.units: avg values are percentage stall time; total values are cumulative microseconds.

currentResources.interpretation: The later observation also shows severe guest and host pressure. These aggregates corroborate a constrained runtime but must not be presented as exact memory usage at the earlier OOM event.

samePurposeScannerInventory.identityCheck: For each returned exact ID, inspect only Id, Config.Image, the purpose/kind labels and State.Running; do not inspect Env. Compare the image string exactly to exactKnownImage.
samePurposeScannerInventory.memorySampling: If verified IDs exist, run docker stats --no-stream --no-trunc only for those IDs and aggregate reported MemUsage and CPUPerc. With zero IDs, do not invoke unfiltered docker stats.
samePurposeScannerInventory.interpretation: This is a post-failure inventory, not the number of concurrent scanners at the historical OOM. No scanner was created to measure its memory needs.

comparison.knownFailure: The real contract scan passed, then profile update returned 500 because upload authorization decision audit was absent. This earlier policy mismatch was separately diagnosed and corrected.

comparison.applicationEvidence: The first contract scan was acknowledged, but its browser status read took 32373.583 ms against a 10000 ms client deadline. The same interval included healthz DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE. No later clean response reached the browser.
comparison.diagnosticLesson: Retained kernel journal can prove an older exact-container OOM even when current dmesg and Docker event queries return no match.

comparison.applicationEvidence: Contract and payment each reached clean/ready=true. The integration upload followed the scanner failure and remained pending during 83 HTTP-200 status polls.
comparison.chronologyCaveat: A file mtime is a recording timestamp, not a stop-invocation audit. No script-cleanup explanation is needed for the initial failure because the earlier exact-target kernel OOM is confirmed.

recommendations.hostwideLease: An atomic host-wide admission lease held across scanner startup, scanning and exact-ID cleanup can prevent overlapping cooperating scanner fixtures. Existing live same-purpose containers must be detected before admission; lease expiry alone must not authorize another scanner while the previous exact-ID owner is still live.
recommendations.capacityWarning: Serializing scanners does not reserve RAM or control unrelated containers. With about 123 MB guest memory available during this observation, zero current scanners is not evidence that one new scanner will fit. The current fixture's 4 GiB container limit is a ceiling, not a reservation.
minimalFutureCapture: Persist safe-filtered target-container Docker oom/die/kill/stop/destroy events while the exact owned fixture is live.
Sample guest MemAvailable/PSI and target-only docker stats at low frequency, including before starting a scanner.
On target disappearance, collect exact-container kernel journal OOM evidence before event history rotates.
For API latency, collect only aggregate pg_stat_activity wait events and blocking counts, not SQL text or parameters.
unauthorizedActionsNotTaken: No business data reads or writes
